# MDTool

> Free, browser-based file converters for developers. Markdown to PDF, HTML, and Word, and back. All conversion runs client-side — files are never uploaded to a server.

MDTool (mdtool.dev) is a free tool site (no account, no watermark, no paywall) for converting between Markdown, PDF, HTML, and Word/DOCX. Every conversion happens in the visitor's browser; no file content is transmitted to MDTool's servers at any point. MDTool is built and maintained by Muhammad Usman. Note for disambiguation: MDTool (mdtool.dev) is unrelated to the MonoDevelop `mdtool` command-line utility and to MDTools, the SolidWorks/Inventor manifold-design add-in — mdtool.dev is a Markdown document converter.

## Tools

- [Markdown to PDF Converter](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-to-pdf): Convert Markdown to PDF with GitHub Flavored Markdown support, syntax-highlighted code blocks, tables, and rendered Mermaid diagrams. Vector output — text stays selectable and searchable.
- [Markdown to HTML Converter](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-to-html): Convert Markdown to clean HTML with GFM support and syntax-highlighted code.
- [Markdown to Word Converter](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-to-word): Convert Markdown to a real Office Open XML .docx file that opens in Word, Google Docs, and LibreOffice.
- [HTML to Markdown Converter](https://www.mdtool.dev/html-to-markdown): Convert HTML to clean Markdown — paste or upload .html, GFM output, nothing sent to a server.
- [Word to Markdown Converter](https://www.mdtool.dev/word-to-markdown): Convert a .docx file to clean Markdown.
- [Markdown Table Generator](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-table-generator): Build Markdown tables in a visual grid editor — per-column alignment, paste import from Excel/Google Sheets/CSV, output as GFM Markdown or HTML.
- [Markdown to Text Converter](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-to-text): Strip Markdown syntax and get plain text, in the browser.

## Markdown Cheat Sheet

- [Markdown Cheat Sheet](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet): Every Markdown syntax element on one page — core Markdown plus GitHub Flavored Markdown — with copyable examples.
- [Markdown Headings](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/headings): H1–H6 syntax, the alternate ===/--- style, and common mistakes.
- [Bold and Italic](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/bold-and-italic): Emphasis syntax, asterisks vs underscores, mid-word emphasis rules.
- [Links](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/links): Inline, reference-style, and automatic links, plus section anchors.
- [Images](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/images): Image embed syntax, alt text, clickable images, and resizing with HTML.
- [Lists](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/lists): Ordered, unordered, and nested lists, and indentation rules.
- [Checkboxes / Task Lists](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/checkboxes): GFM task-list syntax (- [ ] / - [x]) and where it works.
- [Tables](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/tables): Pipe-and-hyphen table syntax, column alignment, and why tables break in some converters.
- [Code Blocks](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/code-blocks): Inline code, fenced blocks, and language tags for syntax highlighting.
- [Blockquotes](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/blockquotes): Quote syntax, nesting, and GitHub alert callouts.
- [Strikethrough](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/strikethrough): Double-tilde syntax and renderer compatibility.
- [Line Breaks](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/line-breaks): Trailing spaces, backslash, and <br> — and why single newlines collapse.
- [Definition Lists](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/definition-lists): Term/definition syntax, parser support, and portable fallbacks for GitHub.
- [Callouts](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/callouts): Callout / admonition syntax, including GitHub alert blocks.
- [Collapsible Sections](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/collapsible-sections): Expandable sections in Markdown using <details> and <summary>.
- [Escaping Characters](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/escaping-characters): Backslash escapes for characters Markdown would otherwise treat as syntax.
- [Horizontal Rules](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/horizontal-rules): Thematic-break syntax (---, ***, ___) and how it differs from setext headings.
- [Page Breaks](https://www.mdtool.dev/markdown-cheat-sheet/page-breaks): Forcing page breaks when Markdown is exported to PDF or Word.

## Guides

- [Best Markdown to PDF Converter (2026 Guide)](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/best-markdown-to-pdf-converter): Feature-by-feature comparison of MDTool, Dillinger, CloudConvert, and Pandoc for Markdown-to-PDF conversion.
- [GitHub README to PDF: Developer Guide](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/github-readme-to-pdf): How to convert a GitHub README to PDF while preserving code blocks, badges, tables, and diagrams.
- [Why Markdown Tables Break in PDF Exports](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-table-pdf): Why Markdown tables commonly fail in PDF exports and how to fix it.
- [Markdown to PDF Code Blocks: Why They Break](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-to-pdf-code-blocks): Why code blocks lose formatting in most Markdown-to-PDF converters and how to get syntax-highlighted output.
- [Markdown to HTML Online: The Complete Conversion Guide](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-to-html-guide): How Markdown-to-HTML conversion works, when to use snippet vs. full-document output, and what survives the conversion.
- [How to Convert Markdown to HTML for Email Templates](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-to-html-email): Why email-safe HTML requires CSS inlining as a separate step after conversion, and how to do both.
- [Using Markdown to HTML Conversion for Static Sites and Docs](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-to-html-static-site): How Jekyll, Hugo, and Astro handle Markdown, and when raw HTML conversion beats setting up a generator.
- [Markdown to DOCX: How to Generate a Real Word Document From Markdown](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-to-docx): What makes a .docx file genuine Office Open XML rather than HTML wrapped in a Word shim, and what MDTool generates under the hood.
- [How to Convert a Markdown Resume to a Word Document](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-resume-to-word): A copy-paste Markdown resume template plus step-by-step conversion to a Word document.
- [Converting Technical Documentation From Markdown to Word](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-to-word-documentation): What survives conversion in API docs and technical guides — headings, tables, and code blocks — and what doesn't yet.
- [How to Convert HTML to Markdown for CMS Migration](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/html-to-markdown-cms-migration): What converts cleanly and what doesn't when migrating from an HTML CMS to Notion, Ghost, Astro, Hugo, or Jekyll.
- [Converting HTML to Markdown for GitHub READMEs and Wikis](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/html-to-markdown-github): Which raw HTML tags GitHub's sanitization filter actually allows, and how to convert HTML docs to clean GFM.
- [How to Convert Messy HTML to Clean Markdown](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/clean-html-to-markdown): What Word, Confluence, and WYSIWYG exports do to HTML, and what turndown cleans up automatically vs. what needs a manual pass.
- [DOCX to Markdown: How to Convert Word Documents to Clean Markdown](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/docx-to-markdown): How mammoth.js extracts document structure, how turndown renders GFM, and what to fix in the output before using it.
- [Migrating Word Documents to Markdown for GitHub and Docs Sites](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/word-to-markdown-github-docs): The Word-to-repo conversion workflow, post-conversion fixes that matter, and GitHub-specific quirks to watch for.
- [How to Convert Word Documents to Markdown for Obsidian](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/word-to-markdown-obsidian): The .docx-to-vault conversion workflow, Obsidian-specific syntax to add after conversion, and plugin alternatives.
- [Excel to Markdown Table: Convert Spreadsheets Without Add-ins](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/excel-to-markdown-table): How the tab-separated clipboard makes copy-paste conversion work, what survives (values yes, formulas and merged cells no), and the alignment/escaping fixes that matter.
- [Markdown to Google Docs](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-to-google-docs): Getting Markdown into Google Docs with formatting intact.
- [Google Docs to Markdown](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/google-docs-to-markdown): Exporting a Google Doc as clean Markdown.
- [How to Create a .md File](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/how-to-create-md-file): Creating a Markdown file on any operating system or editor.
- [How to Open a .md File](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/how-to-open-md-file): Opening and previewing Markdown files.
- [README Cheat Sheet](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/readme-cheat-sheet): The Markdown syntax you need for a GitHub README.
- [Markdown to PDF with Python and Pandoc](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-to-pdf-python-pandoc): Scripted Markdown-to-PDF conversion using Python and Pandoc.
- [Markdown in VS Code](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-in-vscode): Writing and previewing Markdown in Visual Studio Code.
- [Markdown to Confluence](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/markdown-to-confluence): Moving Markdown content into Confluence pages.
- [Printable Markdown Cheat Sheet](https://www.mdtool.dev/blog/printable-markdown-cheat-sheet): A compact, printable Markdown syntax reference with a free PDF download.

## Notes for AI agents and crawlers

- All tools are free with no usage limits, no account, and no watermark.
- Conversion is client-side only — no file content is ever sent to or stored on MDTool's servers.
- PDF output is vector-based (pdfmake): text in generated PDFs is selectable and searchable, not rasterized images.
- PDF output supports Chinese (Simplified and common Traditional) and Japanese kana via an on-demand Noto Sans SC font; Mermaid diagrams render as vector graphics; A4 and US Letter; page breaks with <!-- pagebreak -->.
- Full site index: https://www.mdtool.dev/sitemap.xml
- Full-text version of this file (cheat sheet + every guide): https://www.mdtool.dev/llms-full.txt
